intro:
A transient notification, with a queue and swipe to dismiss.

The queue lives outside React, so `toast.show()` works from anywhere — API clients, event handlers, code with no component around it. `PanelUIProvider` mounts the viewport for you.

Use it for something that happened and needs no response. For a condition that persists on the screen, use [Alert](/docs/components/alert).

parts.Indicator: Status icon, picked from the variant.
parts.Content: Flex-1 wrapper for title and description.
parts.Title: Heading, coloured by the variant.
parts.Action: Trailing action button. Dismisses the toast after its own `onPress`.

notes:
Toasts stack as an overlapping deck: the newest is fully visible and the ones behind peek out, with anything past the third fading rather than accumulating. Swiping toward the edge the toast entered from dismisses it; dragging the other way rubber-bands.

Auto-dismiss durations count visible foreground time: countdowns pause while the app is inactive or in the background, then resume where they left off. `toast.hide(id)` dismisses one, `toast.hideAll()` clears the queue. A `duration` of `0` keeps a toast up until it is dismissed.

examples.title: Firing one
examples.description: Toasts are queued through `useToast`, so any component can raise one without rendering it.

examples.title: With an action
An error you have to dismiss

versions.title: Simple string
versions.description: A string on its own. No title, no description, no action — the whole toast is the sentence, which is what a copy-to-clipboard or a saved-draft actually has to say.

versions.title: With action
versions.description: A title, a description and one thing to do about the result. `actionLabel` draws the control; the toast stays up long enough to reach it.

versions.title: Destructive, top
versions.description: A failure raised at the top edge. `placement` is per-toast rather than per-app, because the edge a message belongs at follows from the message: a result of something you just did belongs near your thumb, and a failure you did not ask for does not.

versions.title: Stack four
versions.description:
Four arriving in turn. Three are visible at once — the newest in front, the rest peeking out behind it — and the deck collapses as each is dismissed.

They are fired a fifth of a second apart rather than together, because the deck is built by things arriving: four on one frame is a stack that was already there.

versions.title: Hide all
versions.description: Clearing the whole queue at once, whatever is in it. Use it when the thing the toasts were about has gone — a screen the user has left, a job they cancelled.

versions.title: Custom component
versions.description: The toast drawn entirely by the caller. The deck still owns its timing, its position and its swipe; `component` only replaces what is inside. `hide` is handed in so a control of your own can dismiss it.
